title: Filtering Basics
description: Add filtering capabilities to your GraphQL API.

data.text: Filtering lets clients narrow results to exactly what they need. Hot Chocolate provides built-in filtering with the `[UseFiltering]` attribute.
Apply `[UseFiltering]` to a query method. Hot Chocolate automatically generates filter input types based on your return type.

data.title: Enable Filtering
data.content: Let clients filter books by any field.

data.text: Hot Chocolate generates a `BookFilterInput` type automatically. Clients can use equality, comparison, and list operators.

data.title: Client Query
data.content: Filter books by price and author name.

data.text: For full control, define a custom filter input type with `[FilterInputType]`.

data.title: Custom Filter
data.content: Define a custom filter with specific fields.

terms.definition: Attribute that enables automatic filter input generation on a query field.
An input type that defines available filter fields and operators.
Operators like eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le for numeric and date comparisons.

data.title: Add Custom Filtering
data.description: Create a BookFilterInput with Title, MinPrice, MaxPrice, and Genre fields, then wire it into the GetBooks query.
steps: Add Title, MinPrice, MaxPrice, Genre properties
Apply Where clauses for each filter
data.expectedOutcome: Clients can filter books by title, price range, and genre in a single query.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Custom filters give you full control
